results.label: this tree ships the plan gate (src/bots/plan-gate.js) (the committed parent does not, and that absence is this probe's control)
the probe renders the states the server really sends: a refused candidate, an ambiguous choice, an auto-selected plan, no plan, and an unreadable stored value
and the refusal the screen has to attribute is a real one: the plan sentence is the FIRST reason on the candidate
the toolbar carries the choice of plan, with `my active plan` as the default rather than a silent pick
and it offers exactly the trader’s ACTIVE plans by name — a paused plan is not a choice the screen makes for them
choosing one re-runs the analysis WITH that plan on the request, so what the screen shows and what the engine checked cannot drift apart
and the request the view then makes names it (`strategy_id`), rather than re-reading a plan it assumed
a running plan is named with the version its rules were saved as, and how many requirements are enforced
the screen says a candidate below is refused BY the plan, rather than leaving the trader to guess why nothing is tradeable
the line that is not machine-checkable is reported as never enforced, and the `require` line the app does not recognise is printed as NOT CHECKED — neither can pass for a checked box
the per-candidate block shows the trader’s own rule text beside its resolved state, with the measured detail that makes the refusal checkable
a plan refusal is attributed on the card even when the trader’s own guardrail owns the action line: both reasons are visible, and the plan is not swallowed by the guardrail message
a requirement whose fact could not be read is rendered as unreadable and says it refused nothing — it never appears as a satisfied box
the plan block adds no control of its own: the gate is explanation, not a second decision surface with its own button
with no active plan the screen says so out loud, tells the trader where a plan is published, and claims nothing was gated
two active plans are named on screen with the way out, and the screen does not pick one for the trader
with one active plan the screen names the plan it used, so the default is visible rather than silent
a stored plan whose rules cannot be read is shown as a plan that needs re-saving — it does NOT render as an empty list of satisfied requirements
an unreadable plan refuses every signal on screen and says every signal is refused until it can be read — a broken read is never shown as a clean, plan-less chart
and a research path that consults no plan says nothing at all, because a research payload is not a claim about a trader’s plan
the editor’s hint is populated on the FIRST open — it does not sit on `loading…` while the trader types the rules it is meant to inform
and it lists the engine’s own vocabulary, line for line, from the server — there is no second copy in the browser to drift out of date
an enumerated fact carries its allowed values on hover, so a trader can write a line the engine will accept rather than guessing
and the hint states the deal: `require` lines are enforced and cannot be overruled, everything else is context that is never interpreted
the Settings alert history names the plan that gated an incoming alert, with the version and how many rules were enforced, and says it REFUSED this alert
and the alert row carries no signal id, so a refused alert is distinguishable from one that became a signal
the alert history endpoint the panel reads is the one it needs, twice (the pane and its own refresh) — not a second source of truth
and the body it sends is an array (one entry per line), which is what the route stores and what the gate parses back — the editor and the gate cannot disagree about the shape

scope: M56 real DOM: the plan, its refusals and the vocabulary a trader edits against: actual runtime/auth/SQL/HTTP with a frozen UTC clock, a synthetic calendar fed through the app's own parser and a patched market module for the thrown-read path; M111 calendar-read states (blocked/clear/unknown), no provider/broker/pixel/human proof and no claim about what a release does to price
